steps: Identify given values: L_0 = 100 cm, \Delta T = 100^\circ C, \Delta L = 0.19 cm.
Use the linear expansion formula: \Delta L = L_0 \alpha \Delta T.
Calculate the coefficient of linear expansion: \alpha = \frac{0.19}{100 \times 100} = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} /^\circ C.
Use the relation between cubical and linear expansion coefficients: \gamma = 3\alpha.
Calculate the coefficient of cubical expansion: \gamma = 3 \times 1.9 \times 10^{-5} = 5.7 \times 10^{-5} /^\circ C.
